speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, what specific antibiotic were you taking when this fever, itchy rash, and joint pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis. The combination of amoxicillin use, low-grade fever, itchy rash starting in flexural areas (antecubital/popliteal fossae), and generalized joint pain is highly suggestive of a severe cutaneous adverse reaction, likely Drug-Induced Hypersensitivity Syndrome (DIHS) or an early presentation of SJS/TEN. This is a medical emergency requiring immediate cessation of the offending agent and hospital admission.
